title: Valuation-ring characterization for a normalized DVR valuation
statement: Let B be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] with fraction field K and normalized valuation v:K^\times\to\mathbf Z. For every nonzero b\in B one has v(b)\ge0. If t\in B is a uniformizer, then v(t)=1 and v(t^{-1})=-1.

source.place: Algebra Definition 00IE (algebra-definition-value-group), valuation-ring and uniformizer properties

proof.text: By the valuation-ring/value-group-Z characterization in [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] (Stacks Definition 00IE), the normalized valuation v has v(b)\ge0 for every nonzero b\in B, and a generator t of the maximal ideal (a uniformizer) has v(t)=1. Since v is a group homomorphism K^\times\to\mathbf Z, 0=v(1)=v(t t^{-1})=v(t)+v(t^{-1}), so v(t^{-1})=-1; in particular t^{-1}\in K^\times.
